video.title: Fantasy Basketball Point Guard Tier Rankings [NBA]

summary: Josh Lloyd ranks fantasy point guards in nine tiers. The tiers are mainly for category leagues, and he gives a Yahoo points league tier for each player too. He warns several times not to build a draft around positional tiers. In fantasy basketball you draft statistical shapes and value, and you only think about positions around rounds 8 or 9. Tier 1 is Luka Doncic and Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, and tier 2 is Cade Cunningham and Anthony Edwards. He is lower than the market on Tyrese Maxey, Jalen Brunson (in categories), Donovan Mitchell and Payton Pritchard. He is higher than the market on Austin Reaves, Coby White, Dejounte Murray, CJ McCollum and Jeremiah Fears. His main point is that leagues are won by getting value against ADP, not by drafting off tiers.

rules.text: Positional tiers can mislead in fantasy basketball. Unlike fantasy football, you do not need to fill positional groups early. Your build changes throughout the draft.
rules.quote: In fantasy basketball, outside of just making sure you've got enough positional cover across your roster, you don't have to do it that way

rules.text: When drafting, look for statistics or statistical shapes, not positions. Positions only become a focus around round 8 or 9.
rules.quote: The position part comes a focus maybe round eight, round nine, you go, "Oh, got to make sure

rules.text: Do not use tier lists as the foundation of your draft. Do not reach for a position because of a drop-off between tiers.
rules.quote: Well, I've got to get a tier one player and now it's a big drop-off, so I've got to target other positions.

rules.text: Use projected usage and minutes as the levers. If you see a player's usage or minutes differently, adjust his ranking to match.
rules.quote: if you disagree with the positioning of a player, you go, "Well, I think he's going to get more usage."

rules.text: Drafting players on the basis that they will not get hurt does not work. Injuries are hard to predict.
rules.quote: if you are drafting someone on the basis of not being hurt, you will get it wrong.

rules.text: He moves players with injury concerns down his rankings even when their per game numbers say they belong higher.
rules.quote: So, with a lot of these injury concern guys, I bump them down. Even though their per game numbers suggest they should be higher.

rules.text: In head-to-head, a player who only plays about two games a week can cost you, even when his per game numbers are good.
rules.quote: picking up Dejounte Murray last season actually cost you leagues. Cuz he literally played two games a week.

rules.text: Do not value players only from last season's ranks. Look at the reasons behind the numbers, such as injuries, limited minutes or a role change.
rules.quote: And this is where if you just base stuff off last season you might as well stick your head up

rules.text: Value a player relative to his draft cost and the players around him. A player you don't like can still be a good pick if he is cheap enough.
rules.quote: Everything in fantasy is about evaluating a player, but then evaluating them in the in the context of everyone else around them.

rules.text: Stats from a team's tanking stretch can understate a player's real value.
rules.quote: some of his numbers last season are hurt by the fact that in the tanking portion of the season

rules.text: Teams coming off a Finals run may have a hangover. Their players are unlikely to repeat the same production.
rules.quote: this is a finals I'll say hangover team. Not necessarily they're going to be bad, but they played two months extra

rules.text: Players can share a tier on median outcome but have very different ceilings. Pick the safe floor or the upside depending on your build.
rules.quote: But based on my median expectation of these players, they're all in the same grouping.

rules.text: Do not let strong steals alone inflate a player's value.
rules.quote: He's going to be very good at steals, so don't let that over inflate his value. Don't get fluffed by it.

rules.text: Draft for value based on ADP, team shape and the risks you have already taken. If you have taken no risks early, take a flyer later.
rules.quote: Hit value based on ADP, based on team shape, based on what you're building. Based on what risks you've taken early.

rules.text: Leagues are won by getting value, like a late pick who outperforms his draft spot.
rules.quote: What wins a league is just getting value. The guy picked 90 becomes the 40th best player.
